newsitem.title: USA: New York City's MAC plans two $400 mln bond sales.
newsitem.headline: New York City's MAC plans two $400 mln bond sales.

text.p: Municipal Assistance Corp (MAC) for New York City said Wednesday it planned to sell $400 million of fixed-rate, tax-exempt bonds in the week of April 21 as part of a big refunding program that began in February.

Further, MAC, which was created in the mid 1970s to rescue New York City from its debt crisis, also plans to sell $400 million of variable-rate, tax-exempt bonds during the first week in May, said an official with the corporation.

"That's it for the fiscal year," said the MAC official, who declined to be named. MAC starts its new, 1998 fiscal year on July 1, and one or two debt sales are planned during that period, though all the details have not been finalized, he said.

J.P. Morgan was selected as the book-running manager, the most lucrative spot on the syndicate, for the fixed-rate bond sale in the week of April 21, while Smith Barney was awarded the top position for the variable-rate debt sale.

MAC's board in late February approved selling $1.4 billion of bonds. In a schedule unveiled then, the MAC said it expected to offer around $390.9 million of fixed-rate bonds in October, through a syndicate led by Goldman Sachs.
And in April 1998, a $230 million sale of fixed-rate bonds was anticipated. That would be followed in April 1999, by a $200 million offering of fixed-rate bonds.
